name: Vite
one_liner: Build tool serving source on demand over native ESM in development, bundling with Rolldown for production.
what_it_is: A build tool that serves source code on demand over native ES modules in development, so dev-server startup is nearly instant regardless of application size, and bundles for production with Rolldown, the Rust bundler that unified its earlier esbuild-and-Rollup pipeline. Framework-agnostic, with a plugin API many frameworks build on.
why_it_matters: Vite is the single most consequential build change since webpack, and the most likely gap in the stack of a developer who stopped re-evaluating tooling around 2019. The difference is not incremental: dev server startup goes from tens of seconds to roughly constant regardless of codebase size, which changes working rhythm rather than just saving time.
suitable_for: Migrating away from slow webpack development builds
Library builds, via its library mode
not_suitable_for: Projects depending on webpack-specific loaders or plugins with no Vite equivalent
Builds needing module federation, where webpack remains stronger
Codebases that must support environments without native ESM in development
